I’ve farmed this land in Quzhou for 15 years, and I know what works on the North China Plain. My 10.1 mu plot feeds my family of five, so I stick to the wheat-maize rotation that’s reliable. With my well, I can irrigate when needed, but diesel for the pump costs money, so I won’t waste water. I’ve got middle school education, which is enough to read seed bags and follow county extension advice, but I trust my hands-on experience more than book learning. Here is what I will do this year:

decision.reasoning_summary: I will plant improved wheat seed in October after rotary tillage, applying compound fertilizer as a base and top-dressing urea at green-up, with three irrigations through the winter and spring to secure a 500 kg/mu yield. Immediately after wheat harvest in early June, I will no-till drill hybrid maize to save time and preserve soil moisture, fertilizing once at sowing and side-dressing at the big-flush stage, irrigating twice during the critical summer period, and spraying for weeds and corn borer to target 550 kg/mu.
